races.name: Weddings At Western House Hotel Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Thistle Nil
runners_data.note: Sole newcomer with strong breeding (U S Navy Flag) making debut for shrewd Goldie yard after lengthy preparation.
runners_data.comment: Sole newcomer in the field and it's a belated debut; likely best watched
runners_data.spotlight: 4yo gelding by U S Navy Flag out of 6f-winning (RPR 74) half-sister to useful winners Taexali (5f 2yo) and Caliburn (7.7f-1m4f); sole newcomer in the field and it's a belated debut; likely best watched.

runners_data.name: Mac's Wee Sister
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare returning after 119-day break, needs pace to aim at and may find this race run to suit.

runners_data.name: Railwayman
runners_data.note: Expensive purchase showed promise last time and similar good going conditions suit his style perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Nicely bred; showed promise with third of 13, behind previous winners, at Leicester
runners_data.spotlight: 420,000gns yearling purchase whose siblings include dual Group 1 sprint scorer Oxted; showed promise with 2l third of 13, behind two previous winners, in Leicester contest (6f, good; wore tongue-tie); respected with progress on the cards.

runners_data.name: Le Puy
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who improved last time out and drops back to a more suitable trip with proven jockey Tudhope.
runners_data.comment: Needs further improvement to get off the mark
runners_data.spotlight: Finished fourth of six at Catterick (7f) on reappearance, managing to improve on her 2yo C&D effort but recording only a modest RPR; needs further improvement to get off the mark.

runners_data.name: Mind Over Matter
runners_data.note: Likely leader returning after 239-day absence but previous form suggests he has the class edge in this grade.

runners_data.name: April Diamond
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare from in-form Jardine yard who needs strong pace and may struggle if Mind Over Matter gets soft fractions.

runners_data.name: Stoneacre Joe
runners_data.note: Gelded since last season and showed dramatic improvement on reappearance, ideally placed to track the leader.
runners_data.comment: One of the main players, provided reappearance effort at Doncaster is backed up
runners_data.spotlight: Gelded after sole 2yo start; belied his 100-1 odds with second of 14, behind clearcut winner, at Doncaster (6f, good to firm) on reappearance; one of the main contenders, provided that form is backed up.

runners_data.name: Wee Dresser
runners_data.note: Limited hold-up horse who lacks the pace to compete at this level and faces impossible task from rear.

runners_data.name: Saxon Gem
runners_data.note: Weak form horse returning after long break, likely needs handicap company rather than maiden level.
runners_data.comment: Always behind in C&D maidens last term
runners_data.spotlight: Always behind in C&D maidens last May/June, beating a total of one rival; likely to find better opportunities in handicaps shortly.

races.paceDynamic: Mind Over Matter is the only confirmed front runner in this field and should get an uncontested lead from the start. Le Puy and Stoneacre Joe will likely track prominently in behind, while the hold-up horses Mac's Wee Sister, April Diamond, Wee Dresser and Saxon Gem will be held up at the rear. With such a sustainable pace scenario and good to firm ground that typically plays fair at Ayr, this race shape strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can position close to the pace from early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Mind Over Matter gets soft fractions and kicks clear approaching the final furlong
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows him to save energy for a strong finish, while the hold-up horses find themselves too far back on ground that won't aid their closing kick. His previous form suggests he has the class edge when conditions suit.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Mind Over Matter sets steady fractions but gets caught flat-footed when the pace quickens
scenarios.body: Stoneacre Joe or Le Puy can use their handy positions to strike decisively in the final two furlongs, taking advantage of the leader's tactical naivety. The prominent racers get the best of both worlds with cover and striking position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes surprisingly strong with multiple horses going forward
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop sets up perfectly for Mac's Wee Sister or another closer to unleash a finishing kick from off the pace. Good to firm ground can sometimes play to patient tactics at Ayr when the pace is genuine.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Newcomer Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Thistle Nil shows natural early speed and races more prominently than expected
scenarios.body: His breeding suggests potential over this trip and being fresh could be a significant advantage in a modest maiden. The Goldie yard knows how to place their horses and this gelding may have been working better than his odds suggest.

watchPoints.text: Watch for Thistle Nil showing early speed in the market - any positive move suggests the Goldie team expect a big run first time out.
Monitor Mind Over Matter's jumping from the stalls - after 239 days off, any sluggish start could compromise his front-running tactics.
Observe Stoneacre Joe's early positioning as his ability to sit handy behind the leader will determine his winning chance.
Check if any of the hold-up horses break faster than expected and force a stronger early pace than anticipated.
Watch for Le Puy getting prominent cover as she needs to avoid being shuffled back from her ideal tactical position.

runners_data.spotlight: 16-race maiden; ran a couple of fair races for Jim Goldie last term after being bought for 10,000gns in July; perhaps best watched after a 181-day break.

runners_data.name: Ski Angel
runners_data.note: Only other prominent runner after 181 days off, could benefit if tracking the leader closely

runners_data.name: Little Mi Mi

runners_data.name: Phil's Dream
runners_data.note: Non-runner

races.paceDynamic: Canaria Queen is the only confirmed front runner and will be allowed an uncontested lead, setting a comfortable pace that suits her style. With most of the field comprised of hold-up horses (Harb, Tommy McJohn, Keep The Gold, Bonito Cavalo, Wee Mary, Royal Duke, Fear And Fast, Little Mi Mi), there will be minimal early pace pressure. Only Ski Angel offers any prominent racing from the pack, but she's unlikely to challenge Canaria Queen for the early lead. This lack of pace pressure strongly favours front runners and prominent racers who can avoid the inevitable late traffic problems that will plague the numerous hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Canaria Queen gets away with soft fractions and kicks clear in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The recent Doncaster winner will have every tactical advantage with no pace pressure, allowing her to dictate terms and find extra when challenged. Her prominent style perfectly suits this race shape with so many hold-up horses needing to come from behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pack of hold-up horses gets bunched up turning for home and several find trouble in running
scenarios.body: Multiple horses will be looking for racing room simultaneously, allowing one or two to find a clear passage and strike. The sheer weight of numbers coming from behind could create enough pressure to reel in the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Ski Angel tracks Canaria Queen closely and has enough left to challenge when the leader tires
scenarios.body: The second prominent runner can sit in the perfect stalking position and time her challenge to perfection. With most others coming from further back, she'll have first run on the leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses gets an unexpectedly prominent position and avoids the traffic
scenarios.body: An early break from typical running style could prove decisive in avoiding the late congestion. This would require a significant tactical switch from connections.

watchPoints.text: Canaria Queen could get away with stealing the race if she's allowed soft early fractions with no pace pressure
Traffic problems are almost inevitable with 8-9 hold-up horses converging simultaneously in the final two furlongs
Tommy McJohn represents an in-form Irish stable making their debut with this yard and could be well-handicapped
Keep The Gold and Royal Duke both return after long absences and may need the run despite previous ability
The claimer-ridden runners Bonito Cavalo and Wee Mary get significant weight relief but face pace disadvantage

runners_data.name: Jkr Cobbler

runners_data.name: Little Ted

runners_data.name: Alex Belardo

runners_data.name: Trais Fluors

races.paceDynamic: Coconut Bay emerges as the sole committed front runner in this field, with Alex Belardo (non-runner) removing the only other prominent runner. This leaves Coconut Bay uncontested on the lead, able to dictate a comfortable pace through the early stages. With seven hold-up horses packed behind him, the pace is likely to be steady rather than fierce, allowing the leader to conserve energy for the final furlong kick. This tactical scenario strongly favors front runners and those able to sit close to the pace, as the hold-up brigade will face a traffic-laden finish when trying to make their challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Coconut Bay Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Coconut Bay gets uncontested lead and finds his rhythm
scenarios.body: Jason Hart can dictate fractions without pressure, saving enough for strong finish as hold-up horses struggle for racing room. His three wins at 7f last summer prove he can execute this tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If no horse challenges Coconut Bay early and pace becomes crawling
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where class and turn of foot matter most, favoring horses with recent good form. Camera Shy and Habrdi have shown best recent efforts despite hold-up styles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Nightmare Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the seven hold-up horses all converge simultaneously in final two furlongs
scenarios.body: Severe congestion creates lottery conditions where only horses with clearest runs can deliver their best. Those drawn wide or with strong finishing jockeys gain crucial advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Coconut Bay Stops Late
scenarios.trigger: If Coconut Bay's 27-day break leaves him short of full fitness
scenarios.body: The leader weakens in final furlong, opening door for closers with most natural pace to pounce. Jkr Cobbler's recent consistency and Camera Shy's class become telling factors.

watchPoints.text: Coconut Bay's fitness after 27-day layoff - any signs of blowing up in final furlong opens race wide up
Traffic congestion in final two furlongs with seven hold-up horses converging - jockey positioning crucial
Ashen's response to first-time Mulrennan partnership and whether Jim Goldie's recent good form continues
Early pace development - if any horse challenges Coconut Bay early it completely changes race dynamics
Camera Shy and Habrdi wearing new headgear for first time - positive or negative response will be telling

races.paceDynamic: Runninsonofagun and Glasses Up will contest the early lead, with both habitual front-runners likely to engage from the start. The honest gallop they create over 1m1f should develop into a strong pace, particularly with Runninsonofagun returning from a 190-day break and Glasses Up showing consistent front-running tactics. Uncle Liam may press from a prominent position early, but the field is dominated by hold-up horses who will look to pounce late. This race shape clearly favours the patient hold-up performers who can benefit from the strong early pace and kick home in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the two front-runners maintain honest fractions and weaken inside the final furlong
scenarios.body: The strong early pace will perfectly set up the race for the patient closers who can unleash their finishing kicks. Royal Blaze, Land Of The Giants, and Dingwall are ideally positioned to exploit the pace collapse.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters gets soft fractions and maintains enough energy for home
scenarios.body: Either Runninsonofagun or Glasses Up could dictate terms if they avoid a speed duel early. The returning Runninsonofagun might benefit from tactical restraint after his long absence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too fast early and completely capitulate in the straight
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish between tired horses, favouring those with the best recent form regardless of style. This scenario brings Dingwall's recent AW form and Land Of The Giants' Cork second into sharp focus.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Profits
scenarios.trigger: If Uncle Liam can secure the perfect tracking position behind the duelling leaders
scenarios.body: The prominent runner gets first run on the leaders while avoiding their pace battle. Uncle Liam's three consecutive seconds suggest he knows how to time his challenge.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Runninsonofagun and Glasses Up engage in a fierce early battle as both are natural leaders who may not yield
Monitor the inexperienced riders on Shifter and Golden Valour in a competitive handicap field
Observe Royal Blaze's early positioning as his hold-up style needs the leaders to go fast enough
Check if Land Of The Giants can transfer his Irish handicap form to this stronger Scottish contest
Watch Uncle Liam's tactics from his wide draw as prominent runners need to secure good early position

races.paceDynamic: Donna Nook is the only confirmed front runner in this seven-runner handicap and should dictate terms from the front without serious pressure. With Pearl Eye, Novak, Eve's Boy, Starliner, Penelope's Sister and Rajapour all preferring hold-up tactics, the pace will likely be steady through the early stages. This creates a tactical advantage for horses that can position prominently or track the leader, as the lack of early pace will make it difficult for pure hold-up horses to find the necessary turn of foot. The race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those capable of getting a good position early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Donna Nook faces no early pressure and controls the gallop
scenarios.body: Daniel Tudhope can dictate fractions and kick clear when it matters, making life difficult for the hold-up brigade behind. The lack of pace pressure allows front runners to save energy for a sustained finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Brigade Rallies
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely steady and multiple closers find racing room
scenarios.body: The patient tactics of riders like Paul Mulrennan and Andrew Mullen pay dividends as their horses unleash finishing kicks. Superior class and ratings overcome tactical disadvantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If a hold-up horse gets closer to the pace than usual
scenarios.body: Eve's Boy or Novak adapt tactics to sit handy behind Donna Nook rather than drop out completely. This hybrid approach allows them to benefit from the steady gallop while avoiding the traffic problems of being too far back.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Donna Nook goes too slowly and the race becomes a sprint from the furlong pole
scenarios.body: The youngest and freshest horses benefit from the tactical muddle as fitness and natural speed override positional disadvantage. Recent runners with sharp finishing kicks thrive in the ensuing scramble.

watchPoints.text: Donna Nook's early position will be crucial - if he drops back rather than leading, the race becomes a crawl that suits nobody
Pearl Eye and Penelope's Sister both return from long layoffs so watch for market confidence and paddock appearance
Connor Beasley's tactics on Eve's Boy given his hold-up style but attractive handicap mark
The pace through halfway - if genuinely slow, expect a mad dash home that could catch out punters backing the leader
Rajapour's headgear effectiveness after looking unlucky but running well in it last time at Wetherby

races.paceDynamic: Iris Dancer is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate proceedings from the start, with no other natural pace pressers to challenge her early. Taygar, Tarlac, The Gay Blade and Filly's Last Lady will all settle prominently behind the leader, creating a compact group through the early stages. The lack of genuine pace competition means Iris Dancer can bowl along comfortably without being harried, potentially setting modest fractions that could play into the hands of those tracking. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can position themselves close enough to strike but avoid doing the donkey work, with hold-up horses Colour Code and Summerstorms Dream facing a tactical disadvantage if the pace becomes pedestrian.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace Suits Trackers
scenarios.trigger: If Iris Dancer dictates at a comfortable tempo without pressure
scenarios.body: The prominent runners get the perfect trip tracking the uncontested leader and have enough left to quicken when it matters. Those positioned second and third can time their challenges perfectly as the lone leader tires.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Gets Away
scenarios.trigger: If Iris Dancer builds an unassailable advantage while others mark each other
scenarios.body: The veteran front runner uses her tactical nous to steal a march while the prominent brigade hesitate, opening up a gap that proves unbridgeable. Her superior course experience and fitness edge carry her home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Helps Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners go too fast trying to track Iris Dancer early
scenarios.body: The compact group behind the leader goes faster than ideal, setting things up perfectly for the hold-up pair to pick up the pieces. Both closers benefit from the strong gallop and superior finishing kick.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Free Running Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Iris Dancer gets completely uncontested fractions and kicks clear
scenarios.body: The experienced mare uses the tactical advantage of racing alone in front to build an insurmountable lead. Her rivals react too late to a horse who has seized complete control.

watchPoints.text: If Iris Dancer breaks smartly and builds a 3+ length lead early, she could steal this race tactically before the field realises the danger.
Watch for The Gay Blade to be positioned perfectly in second or third - his recent wins suggest he's in the form of his life and ready to strike.
If the pace looks pedestrian through halfway, both Colour Code and Summerstorms Dream will struggle to make up ground from their hold-up positions.
Monitor whether Taygar can finally convert consistent placed efforts into victory when getting his ideal race setup behind the lone leader.
Check if Tarlac shows any ring-rustiness early after his 27-day break, as this will determine whether he can capitalise on the favourable pace scenario.

races.name: Book Sounds Of Summer Racenight Handicap

runners_data.name: Elemental Eye
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 60-day break with winning form at longer trips but needs strong pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: Two wins last season, the second by 10l (soft ground); could go well if the ground eases
runners_data.spotlight: Winner at Redcar (2m, good to soft) and Musselburgh (1m6f, soft; by 10l) last term; went hurdling in the winter; fair run back on at Flat at Newcastle in March (1m4f); chance, particularly if the ground eases.

runners_data.name: Tupero
runners_data.note: Class hold-up performer who won last time out but faces tactical disadvantage with no early pace to aim at
runners_data.comment: Ex-French; 1m4f AW winner in February; steps up in trip after below-par run last week
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-French; off the mark at Newcastle in February (1m4f) and a creditable second to a subsequent winner back on turf at Catterick next time (1m4f, good); bit disappointing at Southwell last week, but interesting now up 3f in trip.

runners_data.name: Ebony Maw
runners_data.note: Front-runner and three-time course winner who can exploit the tactical scenario but vulnerable if going too fast early
runners_data.comment: Three wins here, latest over 1m7f; bit to find with Tupero on last month's Catterick form
runners_data.spotlight: Has won three times here, the latest over this trip in October 2024 (good); placed on several occasions without winning last term but was behind Tupero on his reappearance at Catterick last month (1m4f, good).

runners_data.name: Grey Fable
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from small stable making rare appearance, likely to get caught in traffic problems

runners_data.name: Cascade Hall
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 162-day absence for claimer, needs everything to fall right from poor draw

runners_data.name: Aighear
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse and three-time Ayr winner who needs softer ground and typically improves significantly after comeback runs
runners_data.comment: Goes well here (three track wins); best with some give in the ground; may need the run
runners_data.spotlight: Has won three times here, all with give in the ground, twice over this trip; would be interesting if the ground eases but usually comes on for her first run.

races.paceDynamic: Ebony Maw will take this field along from the front as the sole confirmed pace-setter, with the remaining five runners all holding-up horses creating a tactical nightmare. With no pressure on the leader, Ebony Maw can dictate comfortable fractions and kick clear when ready. The lack of prominent runners means the hold-up brigade will be fighting for racing room in the straight, arriving too late. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and early prominent horses who can sit close to the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ebony Maw Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Ebony Maw gets an uncontested lead and dictates moderate fractions
scenarios.body: The 9-year-old course specialist can control the tempo completely and kick clear when the hold-up horses are still finding their legs. His three course wins and recent Ayr victory over this trip make him ideally suited to exploit this tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Traffic Jam
scenarios.trigger: If the five hold-up horses get bunched up and struggle for racing room in the straight
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace means they'll all arrive at once but with limited opportunities to get a clear run. Tupero's class edge from his Newcastle win could see him threading through late to deny the front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Aighear Ground Softens
scenarios.trigger: If the going report is wrong and there's more give in the ground than expected
scenarios.body: The three-time Ayr winner thrives on soft conditions and her trainer Jim Goldie excels with returning horses. She could find significant improvement from her comeback run with easier underfoot conditions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Ebony Maw goes too fast early trying to build an unassailable lead
scenarios.body: The veteran could tie up in the final furlong allowing the stronger stayers like Elemental Eye to pick up the pieces. The 2m winner would relish a truly-run contest over this extended trip.

watchPoints.text: Ebony Maw breaking fast from the gates - if he gets first run uncontested this becomes a procession
The pace through the first mile - if it's genuinely slow the hold-up horses could all arrive together causing chaos
Tupero's position turning for home - his class makes him the main danger if he gets a clear run
Any late market moves on Aighear suggesting the ground is riding softer than official reports
Lauren Young's tactics on Cascade Hall - the 5lb claimer needs to be aggressive early to avoid the inevitable traffic
